issues.text: 'the gap is live today' omits where it is live. At stage-2 the app has no cancel button at all (refund-design.md:61-62 "dù ứng dụng không có nút hủy"; git grep -i cancel stage-2 -- DonHang.App/lib: no match), so the meeting's 'not from the app' already holds there; the gap is the API endpoint only. A reader may infer a customer can cancel a paid order in the app.
issues.quote: but the sample data loaded into the database already holds five `paid` orders, so the gap is live today.
issues.fix: Replace the end with: '…already holds five `paid` orders, so the gap is live today through the API, even though the app at stage-2 has no cancel button.'

issues.text: The lesson attributes the second meaning of `cancelled` to the refund design alone. The design cites YC-5, and YC-5 in the product owner's requirements (refund-requirements.md:36) itself says the refunded order 'chuyển sang `cancelled`'. The business wrote the ambiguous word first; the design follows it. This matters for the lesson's own advice ('agreed with the business').
issues.quote: The refund design, added to the repository after the story, is about to give `cancelled` a second meaning.
issues.fix: In §5, after 'adds a `pending` row to `notifications`.', add: 'YC-5, the product owner's requirement it follows, asks for `cancelled` too.' Optionally in §6 write 'The refund requirements and design, added…'. Add the YC-5 wording to claim 5.

issues.text: The summary of the status-changes lesson told me `Cancel()` is an allowed change 'from `new` or `paid`'. Here the same behaviour is suddenly a gap against the meeting notes. Nothing says the earlier lesson described what the code allows, not what the business decided, so I stop: was the rule I learned wrong, or did the business change its mind?
issues.quote: Yet `Order.Cancel()` refuses only `cancelled` and `shipped` orders, so a `paid` order goes through.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one: 'The status-changes lesson listed `Cancel()` from `new` or `paid` because that is what the code allows; the meeting notes record that the business decided otherwise.'

issues.text: The domain-events lesson I remember says `Cancel()` records `OrderCancelled` after a successful change; I do not remember it refusing a `paid` order. This sentence asks me to recall a check I cannot place, so I cannot confirm the decision 'did reach `Order`'.
issues.quote: by stage-3, the `Cancel()` you read in [[design.l3.domain-events]] refuses a `paid` order, so the meeting's decision did reach `Order`.
issues.fix: Say what the check is: '…refuses a `paid` order with one more `if` that throws, so the meeting's decision did reach `Order`.'

issues.text: This says all four status words come from the story's acceptance criteria, but §4 only tells me the criteria mention `new` and `cancelled`. I take the `paid` and `shipped` part on trust; summary line 2 repeats it.
issues.quote: All four status words of the story's acceptance criteria appear here unchanged
issues.fix: In §4, after 'which then becomes `cancelled`.', add one sentence saying where the criteria also name `paid` and `shipped`.

issues.text: The Vietnamese block and its paraphrase mention a refund row with `paid_at` and a `pending` row in `notifications`. I do not know why a refund has a 'paid' time, or what a `notifications` row is. Neither matters for the main point, but I stopped on both.
issues.quote: one transaction marks the refund row `refunded` with its `paid_at`, moves the order to `cancelled`, and adds a `pending` row to `notifications`.
issues.fix: Add a few words to each: `paid_at` as the time the money was paid back, and `notifications` as the table of messages waiting to be sent (adjust if the repo means otherwise).

issues.text: 'a `paid` order its owner sends there' reads as if the order is sent somewhere. I read it twice to see that the owner sends a request for a `paid` order.
issues.quote: so a `paid` order its owner sends there is cancelled.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'so when the owner of a `paid` order sends this request, the order is cancelled.'
